question:
In a matrix investigation, students select $A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $B=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$. They are asked to examine the inverse of the product $AB$. One student claims that $(AB)^{-1}=A^{-1}B^{-1}$, while another claims that the order of the inverse matrices must be reversed. The students calculate all the required matrices to determine which claim is correct.

(a) Calculate $|A|$ and $|B|$ and determine whether their inverses exist.

(b) Find $A^{-1}$ and $B^{-1}$.

(c) Calculate $AB$ and $(AB)^{-1}$.

(d) Compare $(AB)^{-1}$ with $A^{-1}B^{-1}$ and $B^{-1}A^{-1}$, and identify the correct relation.
explanation:
(a)
$$|A|=\begin{vmatrix}1 & 1\\0 & 1\end{vmatrix}=1$$
$$|B|=\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0\\1 & 1\end{vmatrix}=2$$
Since both determinants are non-zero, both inverses exist.

(b)
$$A^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Also,
$$B^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$

(c)
$$AB=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 1\\1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Now,
$$|AB|=3(1)-1(1)=2$$
Therefore,
$$(AB)^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$

(d)
First,
$$A^{-1}B^{-1}=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}2 & -2\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}$$
This is not equal to $(AB)^{-1}$.
Next,
$$B^{-1}A^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
$$B^{-1}A^{-1}=\frac{1}{2}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1\\-1 & 3\end{bmatrix}=(AB)^{-1}$$
Therefore, the correct relation is
$$(AB)^{-1}=B^{-1}A^{-1}$$

options.D:
(a) $|A|=0,\ |B|=2$
(b) Only $B^{-1}$ exists
(c) $AB=\begin{bmatrix}3&1\\1&1\end{bmatrix}$ is singular
(d) $(AB)^{-1}$ does not exist
